verdict.rationale: PostHog's experiments docs say any captured event can become a funnel, mean, or ratio metric. They also say experiments can measure anything in a synced warehouse table, and external sources can be queried alongside PostHog data with SQL. That covers both data paths in the story without relying on a separate black-box metric store. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of warehouse-based experiment metrics, and detailed docs on how warehouse tables are mapped and joined to experiment exposures.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can define experiment metrics from my own data — warehouse tables or ingested events — instead of a black-box metric store

citations.quote: Any event you already capture can become a funnel, mean, or ratio metric for an experiment.
Measure revenue, subscriptions, or anything else living in a warehouse table you've synced.
Query external data sources (Stripe, Hubspot, Postgres, S3, etc.) alongside PostHog data using SQL.
